text:
maya: heads up — thinking about a rollout pattern for saved views that also wires up telemetry sampling + quota gating. want to avoid surprise spikes and make opt-in for teams. sketch below, thoughts?

maya: problem: users can save per-route/per-model views that trigger heavy telemetry (trace + eval) and we don't want automatic sampling to blow quota or cost. also need smooth rollouts so console changes don't break dashboards.

tj: agree. is this about saved queries generating background evals or just front-end telemetry?

maya: both. saved view can opt into two things: 1) background evals (periodic reruns) and 2) enhanced telemetry (detailed traces for regression detection). we need a single policy that controls sampling rate + quota enforcement per-route.

devon: proposal: attach telemetry_policy to the saved view metadata. policy fields: sampling_rate, max_daily_tokens_quota, rollout_pct, fallback_model. console shows estimated cost.

maya: yep. example config: ```json
{
  "telemetry_policy": {
    "sampling_rate": 0.02,
    "max_daily_tokens": 1000000,
    "rollout_pct": 10,
    "fallback": "gptx-small"
  }
}
```

anita: couple of concerns: 1) where enforcement happens (api gateway vs runtime). 2) what happens when rollout_pct increases mid-run and background evals are queued.

tj: enforcement should be at the router layer (policy check before routing to dedicated/private). we already have token accounting hooks there. runtime can honor sampling decisions from router.

devon: for queued background evals I suggest idempotent checkpoints: eval jobs are scheduled with a telemetry_version tag. if rollout_pct changes, new jobs get new tag; old ones finish but don't count towards new quota.

maya: UI: console should show a tiny badge on saved views: "Telemetry: 2% | Quota 1M tokens/day | Rollout 10%" and a hover explainer with cost estimate and how to disable.

anita: UX note: default should be off for telemetry for orgs on free tier. we can flip on for paid orgs or require explicit opt-in per-team. otherwise support tickets.

devon: implementation checklist: 1) API contract change for saving view; 2) router enforcement hook; 3) background eval scheduler tags; 4) cost-estimation calc in console; 5) rollout metric dashboards.

maya: API shape idea: `POST /api/v1/console/views` payload accepts `telemetry_policy` (optional). Backwards compatible. If omitted -> telemetry disabled.

tj: does the policy need to be org-scoped? i.e., admins can set org-wide max_daily_tokens to cap all saved views from that org.

maya: yes, admins should be able to set org caps and also route-level caps. precedence: org_cap -> route_cap -> view_policy. enforcement is first-hit at router.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/telemetry-policy-gating -> staging -> canary 5% -> scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 PDT. :rocket:

anita: rollout metrics to track: daily tokens consumed by saved views, number of views with telemetry enabled, average sampling_rate, errors from eval jobs, and support churn.

tj: edge case: what if model fallback triggers often? we should expose a per-view health alert and auto-revert telemetry for that view after X failures.

devon: agree. add `auto_pause_on_errors: 3` to policy default. console shows action history.

maya: updated sample: ```json
{
  "telemetry_policy": {
    "sampling_rate": 0.02,
    "max_daily_tokens": 1000000,
    "rollout_pct": 10,
    "fallback": "gptx-small",
    "auto_pause_on_errors": 3
  }
}
```

anita: sounds good. small ask: add a read-only preview API that returns estimated daily cost for a given telemetry_policy so console doesn't guess. `POST /api/v1/console/views/preview-cost` -> {estimated_tokens, estimated_cost}.

maya: will add. next steps: write API PR draft, router hook (tj), scheduler tags (devon), console badge + preview endpoint (anita). i'll own the feature doc and rollout plan.

tj: i'll add router integration ticket. can we gate by plan? will need entitlement check in the API layer.

maya: yes gating by plan. i'll add that to API PR checklist.

devon: thanks — this should keep telemetry useful without surprise bills. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all. I'll post the feature doc in #eng-runtime later today and tag reviewers.
